title: Under the Willow Tree

full_text:
In a quiet village, little Knud and little Johanne grew up as playmates under the shade of an old weeping willow tree. Knud loved Johanne with all his tender heart; they shared gingerbread, sang hymns, and carved their names upon the willow bark.

As youth blossomed, Johanne moved to the royal capital, where her exquisite singing voice won her international fame as an opera prima donna.

Knud, now an honest journeyman shoemaker, traveled across Europe to see her. In Nuremberg, he heard her sing in the great theater. Her voice was like an angel's, but she moved in a world of princes and counts. When Knud spoke with her backstage, Johanne embraced him affectionately as a dear brother from childhood, but showed him her diamond engagement ring, announcing her betrothal to a wealthy nobleman.

Heartbroken, Knud walked out into the snowy night, wandering toward the Alps. Exhausted by grief and frost, he sat down beneath a great weeping willow covered in icicles.

As his eyelids grew heavy, he dreamed that the willow branches turned into golden harps, that Johanne sang only for him, and that they were united in eternal youth. When morning came, peasants found Knud sleeping the sleep of peace beneath the frozen tree, his face radiating the serene joy of an unblemished soul that had found eternal rest.
moral: Unrequited earthly love that remains pure and unselfish finds its ultimate fulfillment in the peace of eternity.
